name: Renal Agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal and Postnatal Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Renal Agenesis

criteria.description: Complete absence of one or both kidneys confirmed by imaging
Absence of corresponding renal artery on Doppler ultrasound or angiography
Compensatory hypertrophy of contralateral kidney in unilateral cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of complete absence of kidney(s) on imaging with absent renal artery; compensatory hypertrophy supports diagnosis in unilateral cases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often made prenatally via ultrasound or confirmed postnatally with ultrasound, MRI, or CT.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral absence of palpable renal tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Detected by imaging or physical examination
searchTerms: no kidney felt on one or both sides
missing kidney tissue on physical exam

pathognomonic.notes: Often the first indication of renal agenesis
searchTerms: absent kidney detected during pregnancy scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent renal artery on Doppler imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Confirms absence of kidney vascular supply
searchTerms: no blood flow in renal artery
absent renal artery detected by imaging

common.notes: Due to decreased fetal urine production
searchTerms: reduced fluid around baby in womb

common.notes: May develop secondary to renal hypoplasia or dysfunction
Indicative of renal stress or damage

occasional.notes: More common in unilateral cases with compensatory hypertrophy
May occur due to chronic kidney disease in bilateral cases
Secondary to severe oligohydramnios in bilateral agenesis
May occur in bilateral renal agenesis due to renal failure

rare.symptomName: Congenital anomalies of the reproductive tract
searchTerms: malformations of reproductive system present at birth

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic kidney disease complications

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen in bilateral cases
imaging: Absent kidney(s) on ultrasound, MRI, or CT scan
Absent renal artery on Doppler ultrasound or angiography
Compensatory hypertrophy of contralateral kidney in unilateral cases
genetic: Mutations in genes involved in renal development (e.g., RET, GDNF) in some familial cases
Association with syndromes such as Potter sequence
other: Oligohydramnios sequence leading to pulmonary hypoplasia in bilateral agenesis
Associated congenital anomalies of the reproductive tract

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cystic, nonfunctional kidney tissue rather than complete absence
Presence of small but present kidney tissue
Reduced nephron number but not complete absence

redFlags: Bilateral renal agenesis with severe oligohydramnios
Pulmonary hypoplasia leading to respiratory failure
references: National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD) - Renal Agenesis
UpToDate: Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract
